items.stem: Whom does the Messenger first address?
options: All who dwell beside the halls of Cadmus
The king's guards at the gate of the tomb

items.stem: According to the Messenger, what casts down and raises high and low alike?
Complete Creon's cry as the Messenger reports it: “Is this the saddest _____ I ever trod?”
To which goddess was Eurydice going to pray?
What does Eurydice say happened when she heard the wail?
options: She fainted in her handmaids' arms
She ran at once to the tomb outside the city
She laughed at the Messenger's tale

items.stem: What did Creon's men pile up for Polyneices?
How does Eurydice leave after the Messenger's tale?
What does Creon call himself near the end?
options: A great and glorious king of Thebes

items.stem: What does the Messenger mean by “none can read a mortal’s horoscope”?
options: No one can know a person's future
The stars are hidden by clouds over Thebes

items.stem: Complete the Messenger's line: “Truth is ever _____.”
What do the Messenger and the elders fear about Eurydice's silence?
options: It may hide some fell design
It shows she did not hear the news
It shows she blames the guard

items.stem: What does Creon mean by “By sorrow schooled”?
options: He was trained in a school

items.stem: Why does the Messenger insist on telling the whole truth?
options: Flattery would be proved false later
He wants a large reward from the queen herself

items.stem: What is the tone of Creon's lines “Alas, my son, Life scarce begun, Thou wast undone”?
What does the Chorus say Creon bears with him as he enters?
options: Gifts for the gods of Thebes
A new decree for the city

items.stem: What does Creon mean by “every way Leads but astray”?
options: He has nowhere left to turn
He has lost his way home in the dark

items.stem: What does the Messenger's phrase “The shadow of a shade” suggest about wealth without joy?
Complete Creon's line: “Humbled my pride, my pleasure turned to _____”
What is ironic about Creon's cry in line 1152?
options: He now fears the very warning he had mocked
He has become a priest of Apollo
He is glad to hear his son's voice
He has forgotten what the seer said to him long ago

items.stem: Why does the play report the scenes at the tomb through a Messenger?
options: It keeps the focus on Creon's reaction and loss
The Messenger is the true hero of the whole play
Creon is not allowed at the tomb
The tomb is in another city

items.stem: What does the Chorus's “Too late thou seemest to perceive the truth” emphasize?
options: Recognition has come after the damage
Creon has learned nothing at all

items.stem: What does the Messenger mean by the halls of Death in lines 1180–1181?
options: Their marriage takes place only in death
Creon has built a new palace
The wedding feast was held in the palace

items.stem: How has Creon changed by the end of the play?
options: He accepts guilt instead of defending his will
He blames Antigone and the elders for his many losses

items.stem: What does the Chorus's “Swelling words of high-flown might Mightily the gods do smite” warn against?
How does the Messenger's opening on “Fortune with a constant ebb and rise” frame the news?
options: As proof that no one's luck is secure
As a punishment sent by Antigone's ghost
As a story of good luck
As a warning about the sea

items.stem: Complete Creon's line: “Heavy the hand of _____”
What is ironic about the Chorus's earlier praise of man's skill in light of the ending?
options: Man's cleverness could not save Creon from folly
The Chorus has long distrusted man's skill and daring

items.stem: What does the Messenger's moral “Mortals’ unwisdom is the worst of all” add to the account?
options: It turns the report into a lesson about folly
It praises the dead for their wisdom
It blames the gods and Fortune for the deaths in the palace

items.stem: How does Creon's final speech echo Antigone's earlier laments?
options: He too laments that he is undone and asks to be led away
He praises the power of the State and its laws, as Antigone once did
He defends his edict as Antigone defended hers
He leaves Thebes as she left the city

items.stem: The final lines, ending “Wisdom brings to age at last”, suggest that wisdom
options: Comes through suffering, often too late
Is given freely to the young
